title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'DJ Turn Me Up', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the mic: black handheld vocal mic (held at the chin, on the stand); the mic stand: chrome straight stand on a round base, waiting at the far end of the room (waiting far off, gripped on the beat, held through to the end); the daisy: white daisy with a yellow centre and exactly eleven petals (eleven petals, counting down, bare stem, stem dropped); the wedding bands: a pair of plain gold wedding bands, enlarged on the projection (interlocked, sliding apart, far apart); the projection wall: wall-sized projection on painted brick behind the bar showing the line's images (vineyard ghosts, diverging rings, trucked house, three roads, blank glow); the decks: two-deck controller with crossfader and glowing faders, a vinyl on a turntable, headphones (scratch, fader up, master to the top); the bar: home bar of dark wood with neon underglow, bottles behind (petals on it); lighter: plastic lighter, lit (raised); phone: smartphone, screen lit (raised). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
